tags.description:
Bills of Lading

The Bills of Lading endpoint provides access to shipping documents that serve as a receipt for cargo and a contract of carriage between the shipper and carrier. These documents contain detailed information about the cargo, vessel, parties involved (shipper, consignee, notify party), and origin/destination locations.

Practical Information:

  • All date/times within this endpoint are presented in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
  • Bills of Lading are available for US Import and US Export shipments.
  • Each bill of lading is linked to a specific port call and contains cargo and vessel details.
tags.name: BillsOfLadings

tags.description:
Trade, Voyage, and PortCall IDs are prefixed by commodity type to ensure uniqueness across all datasets.


This change follows the merge of all commodity APIs (LNG, LPG, Dry Bulk, and Liquids) into a single unified API available at api.kpler.com/v2.


This represents a major improvement in user experience, allowing users to access all commodities through one consistent endpoint instead of managing four separate URLs.


For users migrating from the v1 API, the new IDs are derived by adding the commodity prefix to the former v1 ID (i.e., new_id = prefix + v1_id).


Prefix mapping:

  • 1 - LNG
  • 2 - LPG
  • 7 - Dry Bulk
  • 8 - Liquids (Crude/CO, Chem/Bio, DPP, Clean Products)

As an example for LNG Commodity Type,

  • v1 API id: 234234
  • v2 API id: 1234234

Trades

This endpoint provides users with comprehensive access to commodities flows at a granular trades level. Trades represent commercial operations centered around the cargo and involve key entities such as buyers, charterers, and sellers. It's important to note that in the case of Ship-to-Ship (STS) transfers, multiple vessels may be involved.

  • All date/times within this endpoint are presented in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
  • A trade commences with the conclusion of the origin Port Call, and concludes either when the vessel reaches the berth at the destination Port Call or when the vessel departs the port if the installation is unknown.
tags.name: Trades

tags.description:
Flows

The Flows endpoint serves as an aggregation of trades, offering a macro-view of individual cargoes in real-time. This pivotal endpoint provides users with a holistic perspective, allowing them to quickly identify trends in the commodities market.

Directional Analysis

Users have the flexibility to analyze flows based on the direction of cargo movement—be it imports, exports, or net flows.

Granular Splits

The Flows endpoint empowers users with the capability to perform multiple splits based on various parameters, including origins, destinations, products, routes, and more. This granularity facilitates in-depth analysis and trend identification.


Practical Information:

  • All date/times within this endpoint are presented in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
  • Split Granularity: You can apply up to 5 splits simultaneously. For more granularity, we would suggest using our /trades endpoint.
tags.name: Flows

tags.description:
Port Calls

The Port Calls endpoint offers detailed cargo-by-cargo information for loading and discharging activities occurring at specific points of interest, including installations and zones. Each port and terminal zone is meticulously defined by Kpler, and the system automatically generates a port call as soon as a vessel enters the designated zone.

Load and Discharge Details

Loads are represented with a positive quantity, while discharges are indicated by a negative quantity. This distinction provides clarity on the nature of cargo movements within each port call.

Canal Crossing Detection

Port calls play a crucial role in detecting canal crossings, providing insights into vessel movements through navigational channels.

Practical Information:

  • Port calls can exist in the past, present, or future, allowing users to analyze historical data, monitor ongoing activities, and plan for upcoming cargo movements.
  • Ship-to-Ship (STS) transfers are treated as port calls, capturing the dual nature of these operations—acting as a load for one vessel and a discharge for another.
  • Arrival and departure times are computed based on AIS (Automatic Identification System) positions received from vessels, ensuring real-time tracking accuracy.
  • All timestamps are presented in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
tags.name: PortCalls

tags.description:
Fleet Metrics

The Fleet Metrics endpoint offers a comprehensive view of both global and regional trends by aggregating fleet data. This powerful tool provides valuable insights into impactful trends within the markets, allowing users to make informed decisions based on a holistic understanding of fleet dynamics.

Floating Storage

This analysis focuses on laden vessels that have been floating for a minimum of 7 days for liquids and at least 1 day for LNG. It provides insights into vessels in a state of suspended operation, offering a unique perspective on market conditions.

Commodities On Water

This analysis encompasses the total amount of commodities carried by vessels, regardless of their state—whether in motion or stationary. It includes both actively moving vessels and those engaged in floating storage. This comprehensive view aids in understanding the overall volume of commodities at sea.

Practical Information:

  • All date/times within this endpoint are presented in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
  • Among the two types of analysis we can provide granular data through aggregation.
tags.name: FleetMetrics

tags.description:
Ship to Ship

The Ship-to-Ship (STS) endpoint provides detailed information about operations where one vessel serves as the terminal, facilitating the transfer of cargo to another vessel. This dynamic operation involves an unloading vessel delivering cargo to a loading vessel, with the latter mooring to the former.

Practical Information:

  • All date/times within this endpoint are presented in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
  • Among the two types of analysis we can provide granular data through /vessels or aggregated data.
tags.name: ShipToShips

tags.description:
Diversions

The Diversions endpoint provides access to historical and current vessel diversions for all LNG vessels. A diversion occurs when a vessel changes its intended destination, providing insights into market dynamics and operational changes in the LNG shipping industry.

Practical Information:

  • All date/times within this endpoint are presented in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
  • Diversions track changes from the original destination to a new destination, including information about origin, diverted-from location, and new destination.
  • You can filter diversions by vessel state (loaded or ballast), charterers, cancelled zones, and cancelled installations.
tags.name: Diversions

tags.description:
Products

The Products endpoint provides access to Kpler's product taxonomy and hierarchy. This reference data helps users understand how commodities are classified and can be used for filtering in other endpoints.

Product Hierarchy

Products are organized in a hierarchical structure with four levels: Families > Groups > Products > Grades. Each level provides increasing specificity, from broad commodity families down to specific product grades.

Practical Information:

  • This is static reference data that does not change frequently.
  • Use product names from this endpoint to filter trades, flows, and other cargo data.
  • The hierarchy helps in aggregating or drilling down into specific commodity categories.
tags.name: Products

tags.description:
Contracts

The Contracts endpoint provides access to Kpler's contract data, including details such as contract dates, zones, installations, and more. This endpoint is useful for understanding the terms and conditions of cargo transactions.

Practical Information:

  • All date/times within this endpoint are presented in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
  • You can filter contracts by date range, zones, installations, and more.
  • This endpoint only allows retrieving LNG and LPG contracts. Only these 2 commodities are covered.
tags.name: Contracts

capacity.description: Maximum capacity of the vessel in the unit stated in the field.

tankTechnology.description: Pressurization and refrigeration information of the vessel''s tanks classified as semi or fully refrigerated tanks. Applicable for Gas carriers only

owner.description: Company currently owning the vessel. The ownership is assumed by the charterer or mother company in case of time or spot charter.

type.description: Vessel classification based on the deadweight of the vessel.

imo.description: The International Maritime Organization (IMO) unique identifier for the vessel.

capacity.description: Maximum capacity of the vessel in the unit stated in the field.

name.description: Name of the zone. Zone can refer to any of the geographical tree hierarchy.

installation.description: Name of the installation where the diversion occurs.

zone.description: Name of the zone where the diversion is taking place.

portCallId.description: KPLER identifier for the port call associated with the diversion.

date.description: Date and time when the diversion occurred.

Quantity.description: Volume of the product traded in the unit of measure stated by the field.

CargoProduct.description: Name of the commodity/product represented in our family tree. Family, Group, Product, Grade. Examples include Crude, Gasoline, FO.

id.description: KPLER identifier of the most granular product on the trade(Grade, or Product/commodity, or Group, or Family).

name.description: The platform provides access to our product offering within Dirty, Clean products, LNG, LPG and DRY platform

sulfurContent.description: Sulfur content of the product, expressed in mass percent.

apiGravity.description: API gravity of the product. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API_gravity

id.description: Kpler identifier of the parent zone.

zoneType.description: Type of the parent zone (Port, Country, Region, ...).

ProductWithEstimation.description: Name of the commodity/product represented in our family tree. Family, Group, Product, Grade. Examples include Crude, Gasoline, FO.

charterer.description: A charterer is an entity that hires or leases a vessel from a shipowner for the transportation of commodities.

location.description: Name of a port where the operation occurs.

zone.description: Name of the geographical area/location associated with the event. This field can refer to any of the location in the hierarchy tree e.g.continent, country etc

country.description: Country where the operation occurs, the countries follow ISO standards.

subcontinent.description: Name of the subcontinent where the port call is taking place.

continent.description: Name of the continent where the port call is taking place.

forecast.description: Boolean. True if this port call has been forecasted automatically by our system

floatingDays.description: The number of days the vessel has been floating.

floatingSince.description: Date indicates since the vessel started Floating.

stsStartDate.description: A STS is an operation and thus has a duration. This is the start date of the first STS operation taking place in the trade.

loadVesselEta.description: Estimated Time of Arrival of the daughter vessel at the anchorage area to conduct the STS. During a STS, one vessel is discharging its cargo into another vessel. The first is the mother and the second is the daughter.

stsEndDate.description: A STS is an operation and thus has a duration. This is the end date of the first STS operation taking place in the trade.

dischargeVesselEta.description: Estimated Time of Arrival of the mother vessel at the anchorage area to conduct the STS. During a STS, one vessel is discharging its cargo into another vessel. The first is the mother and the second is the daughter.

loadPortCallId.description: KPLER identifier of the port call of the loading vessel in the STS operation.

dischargePortCallId.description: KPLER identifier of the port call of the discharging vessel in the STS operation.

loadVoyageId.description: KPLER identifier of the voyage of the load vessel involved in the sts operation

dischargeVoyageId.description: KPLER identifier of the voyage of the discharge vessel involved in the sts operation

name.description: Name of the vessel involved in the diversion.

imo.description: The International Maritime Organization (IMO) unique identifier for the vessel.

mmsi.description: The Maritime Mobile Service Identity of the vessel (9 digits)

type.description: Vessel classification based on the deadweight of the Vessel

capacity.description: Maximum capacity of the vessel in the unit stated in the field

allOf.description: Name of the zone where the cargo is being loaded/unloaded. Zone can refer to any of the geographical tree hierarchy.

Name of the installation where the cargo is being loaded/unloaded. It can be unknown if it is a future port call, a STS or if we couldn't determine the installation in the port due to lack of positions.

id.description: Shipment id, Kpler identifier for mono-product trade, tracking evolution of the commercial information.

parentId.description: Shipment id, Kpler identifier for mono-product trade, tracking evolution of the commercial information.

country.description: Name of the country where the STS in the trade is taking place.

startDate.description: A STS is an operation and thus has a duration. This is the start date of the STS operation taking place in the trade.

endDate.description: A STS is an operation and thus has a duration. This is the end date of the STS operation taking place in the trade.
